newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINLAND REJECTS EU BAN ON TAX-FREE XYLITOL.
newsitem.headline: FINLAND REJECTS EU BAN ON TAX-FREE XYLITOL.

text.p: The Finnish government on Tuesday formally rejected a European Commission decision to deny it the right to give tax-exempt status to xylitol, a sweetener made of birch trees and used in confectionery.

"The government of Finland rejects the EU Commission's note in which it maintains that the tax-exempt status of xylitol sweets in Finland is against the law of the European Union," the government said in a statement.
Finland said the tax exemption on xylitol was not against EU law because it had public health-related goals.

The European Commission said in December it would ban tax relief for xylitol in Finland because it suspected this constituted hidden support for Finnish xylitol maker Xyrofin, a unit of food ingredients group Cultor .
It delivered a note to Finland in April stating its position, as the first stage in a review process.
The Finnish government said its law did not distinguish between goods manufactured in Finland or elsewhere: tax-free status did not benefit sweets only made in Finland.
The government also rejected the Commission's view that xylitol sweets had gained a significant market share in Finland due to the tax exemption.

Xylitol chewing gum already had a 94.7 percent share of the Finnish chewing gum market before the tax relief was granted and there had been major growth in xylitol sweets' market share since, the government said.
The government said its response to the Commission had listed 43 studies backing its position and demonstrating the beneficial dental health effects of xylitol.
It said it had also asked for a statement from international experts on the subject.
Finnish food groups Cultor and Huhtamaki in April said an EU ban on xylitol's tax exemption would not be not materially significant to their companies.
